description:
## Failure

Observed on main (0.7.2) in a three-node MinIO-backed cluster (../bedrock_ex harness, three_node.sh). Code path is identical on origin/develop (3af051c2).

`Coordinator.Server.init/1` loads `prior_core_state` from the object-storage bootstrap exactly once. After that it changes only in `handle_cast({:notify_transaction_system_layout, tsl, core_state})`, which the Director sends to ITS OWN coordinator — the raft leader. Followers keep whatever they loaded at boot. When a follower later wins leadership, `handle_info({:raft, :leadership_changed, {me, _}})` -> `attempt_director_recovery(:leadership_change)` hands the Director that boot-time value.

Two consequences, both reproduced:

1. **Wipe (follower booted on a fresh cluster, prior_core_state = nil).** c3 booted before any bootstrap existed. Later the leader died (it held the only log). c3 won the election: `CoreState.fresh?` -> "Initializing a brand new system", recruitment "replaced log candidates that failed to lock [g27rspgg] with fresh workers [ze74geya]", "Fresh cluster detected, using default shard layout", recovery completed at epoch 4 and PersistencePhase wrote a NEW bootstrap (new cluster_id, logs [ze74geya]) over the real one. The committed data now lives only in the orphaned log on the dead node's disk; every later cold boot loads the empty epoch-4 system. The same wipe happened once spontaneously after an unexplained election (see the election-flapping ticket).

2. **Stale (follower booted at epoch N, cluster moved to N+1).** c2 booted while the bootstrap named log rbj74rpq; recovery at epoch 2 retired it in favor of g27rspgg. When c2 later led, its Director waited for a quorum of rbj74rpq — a log that will never exist again.

## Expected

The Director launched on a leadership change must start from the latest durable core state — the bootstrap in object storage at that moment (FDB: the new cluster controller reads DBCoreState from the coordinators at recovery start, never from its own memory). A nil/absent durable record must not be conflated with a follower that simply never learned the current one.

## Repro sketch

Unit level: start a coordinator as follower with no bootstrap, let a Director on another coordinator persist a bootstrap, then deliver `{:raft, :leadership_changed, {my_node, term}}` and assert the launched Director receives the persisted core state (not nil). Live: ../bedrock_ex three_node.sh — boot all three fresh, kill -9 the leader, repeat until the node that booted fresh wins.
title: [BUG] A follower coordinator that wins leadership launches recovery with its boot-time prior_core_state: a stale nil re-initializes the cluster and overwrites the bootstrap
